name: Owl
intro: An owl is a bird with big round eyes. Most owls are awake at night.

sections.title: What does it look like?
sentences: Owls are birds with big round eyes.
Their eyes can not move around.
So an owl turns its whole head to look.
Owls have sharp claws called talons.
The smallest owl is about as big as a soda can.

sections.title: Where does it live?
sentences: Owls live almost everywhere on Earth.
Some owls live in forests, and some live in deserts.
Snowy owls live where it is very cold.
Burrowing owls live in holes in the ground.
Many owls nest in tree holes or old nests.

sections.title: What does it eat?
sentences: Owls are predators.
They eat mice, insects, and small birds.
Some owls catch fish.
Owls have no teeth.
They cough up pellets of bones and fur.

sections.title: How does it grow?
sentences: A mother owl lays eggs.
Owl eggs are white and almost round.
Baby owls hatch from the eggs.
The mother takes care of them for about three months.
At about six months old, they look like their parents.

sections.title: Fun facts
sentences: Most owls are nocturnal.
Owls fly with almost no sound.
An owl can hear a mouse step on a twig far away.
There are more than 200 kinds of owls.
An owl can turn its head most of the way around.

vocab.meaning: Awake at night and asleep in the day.
An animal that hunts other animals for food.
The sharp claws on a bird's feet.
A small ball of bones and fur that an owl coughs up.
